function: Beam prediction: selects the best of 64 codebook beams from camera, LiDAR, radar, and GPS inputs (BeamTransFuser), with pruning for latency and a CVAE filling missing modalities (p. 4, 6).
system: RSU with uniform linear array and 64-beam codebook; vehicle with omnidirectional mmWave transmitter; RSU sensors camera, LiDAR, radar, GPS; no RIS (p. 3, 6, 11).
method: Supervised Transformer multi-modal fusion with ResNet branches, focal loss, 30 epochs; KL-based pruning plus fine-tuning; separately trained CVAE for missing modalities (p. 5-10, 11).
data_channel: DeepSense 6G measured multi-modal dataset, urban scenarios 31-34 (day and night): 11,243 samples with 64-beam received-power labels; 90% training, 10% validation (p. 11).
test_conditions: Trained on 90% of pooled scenarios 31-34, validated on the other 10%; trained model also tested with radar or LiDAR missing (zero-filled, noise, or CVAE-generated) (p. 11, 13).
baselines: All learned: Avatar, position-based and multi-modal models of [11], TII, CMDF, QTNs, ICMFE, MMDL, MMT; missing-modality variants zero-filled, noise, modality dropout; no non-learned method (p. 11, 13).
metrics: DBA-score, Top-1/2/3 accuracy, inference latency on three GPUs, DBA versus remaining parameter ratio, Top-k under missing modality (p. 11-13).
complexity: 78.42 M parameters (Table II); pruning to 0.4-0.9 of parameters; inference latency on GTX 1080, RTX 4070Ti, L20; CVAE adds about 17 ms (p. 7, 12-13).
openness: none; only the public DeepSense 6G dataset is used, no code link (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 11: "DeepSense 6G provides synchronized multi-modal data collected from real-world vehicular communication scenarios" - measured data, scenarios 31-34.
q2_support: p. 11: "split the dataset into 10,118 (i.e., 90%) samples for training and 1,125 (i.e., 10%) samples for validation" - held-out part of pooled scenarios 31-34; missing-modality tests (p. 13) corrupt inputs at the same site.
q3_support: p. 11: "We include all existing methods that utilize the same dataset" - Avatar, TII, QTNs, MMT and others are all learned; no non-learned method is compared (exhaustive search only mentioned, p. 7).
q4_support: p. 12: "We further evaluate the inference latency across three hardware platforms" - plus 78.42 M parameters in Table II (p. 7).
q5_support: p. 11: "As a publicly available and widely used multi-modal dataset, DeepSense 6G" - trained and tested on it; no code link of its own.
notes: Included, area 5 rather than 3: the paper frames the RSU system as ISAC (sensing-assisted predictive beamforming, p. 1 and 3) and 5 precedes 3 in the tie-break; area 3 is the alternative if read as communication-only beam selection. q2=0 is borderline: only the missing-modality test (p. 13) is outside training inputs. q3=0: Position-based [11] is not described as non-learned.
